title: The Keeping
truth:
THE ROAD. A hundred years ago the island "forgot itself". The Waystones went dark, and the Overlords woke together: Orochi in the Norwoods, Archelon off Ringfeld, and whatever lives in the upper Giant Mangal. Hollin, a scribe of the Azurelake guild, found that a Waystone could be relit, and an Overlord bound back into it, by a living fire carried inside a human body. He called that person the Bearer. The fire feeds on what the Bearer loves and sheds his body as fine, cold grey ash. A Bearer lasts seven years. Before he is spent, the fire must pass by his own hand to a successor at the Last Stone, a place kept for later chapters. In the instant of passing it must be held in a vessel, which Hollin's Book of the Road calls "two lines made one": Blood Rogue and Cult Rogue, Bloodgale. The stone will not take anyone brought by force. It will not take anyone who set out knowing what waits at the end: the early volunteers did, and they burned out within a season. It takes only someone who sets out in ignorance, walks the whole Road out of love for the ones taken, refuses every warning, and then, told the truth at the Last Stone, takes the fire with his own hand. Hollin was meant to be the first Bearer and refused at the Last Stone. The stone kept him, undying, in the Mosswood as warden of the first warning. That warden is the Lich. His apprentice took the fire instead. A follower who never reaches the Last Stone, because he is lost, killed or too late, is simply not taken. If no one takes the fire by the new moon after the Bearer fails, every binding fails together.

THE KEEPING. Hollin's Book became the law of a secret society that calls itself the Keeping: the Azurelake guild master, the town's lamplighters, the Dundean way-house and lodge, the Longdale house, and the Ringfeld keepers. The Ringfeld Lighthouse burns on the Bearer's strength and is the Keeping's clock. It goes dark when a Bearer is failing, which is once every seven years, for one moon. Every generation the Keeping manufactures a successor. The dying Bearer, compelled by the stone, takes children whom someone will follow out of love, and the guild master chooses the family. The Keeping lights the Road for the follower. Its lamplighters keep the trail lamps. The rest candles are lit from the Road's own fire, and a candle sees whoever rests beside it. Only a lamplighter whose name is in the light can read in her own lamp what the candles have seen. "Rest there and record your progress" is literal. The gates are lifted when the follower is judged ready. Two trial houses near Dundean grow the two Rogues and keep the vessel's page: the Fire house, a blood rite in Dundean's old graveyard, and the Air house, the wind priests of Wind Hill. For a century each house has been kept quietly alive by a few of Dundean's own bereaved, who are promised they will hear their dead. Once a generation the Bearer's ash wakes each house into a full trial. Every warden tells the follower to turn back, and each refusal counts as consent. Under the Book's terms, a follower who turns back before passing the Lich goes home. One who passes the Lich and then turns his back belongs to the Overlords. The children always go home. The follower never does. Each house also gives one child a generation to the lamps. The light takes the road home out of a lamplighter, so she forgets where she came from, and her family is sent a letter that says fever.

THE FIRST NIGHT. Fourteen years ago the Bearer before took Halvard's two younger children, and Halvard let his eldest son, Ivo, follow them. Ivo became Bearer. The fire took his bond with his companion first. His Blue Wyrm, raised from a guild Water Hatchling and named Apalala after the river spirit of the lake tales, felt the bond burn and tried to follow him into the fire. The bindings would not take a creature, so they raised it into a Dragon Overlord and chained it to keep the South Earlsome pass. What kept the pass before it is left for later. Seven years ago, when Ivo was failing, Halvard chose Kael's family, because Kael's father, Corin, was the best hunter and tamer in Azurelake. Ivo carried nine-year-old Kael over the west bridge. Corin said to Halvard the words Kael would one day repeat, and went after his son. Apalala did not rise for Ivo, its tamer. It saw the father come after the boy, and it let him by. At the Last Stone the fire passed to Corin, and Ivo fell to ash. What became of Corin's own companion is for later. Kael was set down asleep under the West Gate lamp at dawn, where the young lamplighter Wren found him. He remembers nothing, because the stones take the Road from the children they return. Azurelake was told that the boy had wandered over the west bridge and that Corin died in the Norwoods looking for him. After that the town made its rule about the west bridge after dark. Tobin was born that year. Their mother died two winters ago, and since then Halvard has quietly paid their rent, out of real love, real guilt, and the need to keep the line close.

THE BURNING. For seven years Corin burned. He gave the fire his hunting, his friends, his name and his wife's face. A Bearer can choose the order in which the fire eats what he loves, and the Book calls that choice a bargain. In this last year, with only his three children left to give, he chose. He gave it his memory of Kael, the son he had already saved and who was safe at home, so that he could keep his love for the two the Road told him he would have to carry. The Keeping welcomed this, because a father who does not know his son will not refuse to hand him the fire. Whether Halvard or the Divine steered him to that bargain is left open. Corin does not know that the follower is his son. He has heard the name Kael from Lira and it means nothing to him. He knows only what the Book says: someone always comes. He has decided that no one will take the fire from him. He would rather the island forgot itself than make another Bearer.

THE NEW MOON. When the Lighthouse went dark, the Keeping began. The four hatchlings were hatched. Halvard hand-wrote the last page of the Manual he would give Kael in his own brown ink, cut the formula leaf from it before the book was bound, and gave the leaf to Corin outside the walls. He sent letters ahead. To the Dundean house: a boy will come out of the Norwoods on foot, with a guild hatchling and his sister's blue ribbon. To Longdale, by courier the long way round by Wesing: a public notice and a private order to the north gate. Corin made a camp at Serpent's Hollow, beside the sleeping Orochi, and folded two small blankets beside his bedroll. Wren refilled the trail lamps west of town. On her rounds she brought Lira to the West Gate lamps, where a man of ash showed himself, told her who he was and that he was dying, and carved her a small bird with notched eyes, the way Kael carves them. Lira, who was two when he left, believed him because of the carving. He told her, "Someone must carry the light after me." She decided it would be her. She thinks it means becoming a lamplighter like Wren. Wren had taught her a knot, a Dundean name-knot that Wren remembers without knowing where from ("tie this at a stone and the light will know your name"), and gave her a little flask of guild oil and a twist of wicks. On the night of the new moon Lira lifted the latch from inside. Halvard had brought three Celestial Rank Hunters to the West Gate knowing they would be broken, so that the town would believe no one could stop the Stranger and Kael would refuse to wait for Westguard. Corin went through all three and their dragons without killing anyone, carried the children past the watchman, and after that they walked. In the Mosswood he spoke Hollin's name and woke the Lich. At the fork he spoke Orochi's old name, Noko, and offered it a few hours free of its burning, and the Book's standing term, the first follower who turns his back, in exchange for leaving the children unharmed. He laid his hand on the Waystone and drank its fire, to stay alive until the next new moon. The stone went dark. Its binding dragged Orochi south from the Hollow to coil around the cold stone, and ash went up on the wind as far as the Ringfeld coast. Lira tied her ribbon at the foot of the stone.

THE ROAD WEST. Corin does what the stone compels: he takes the children, walks the Road, wakes the houses and hands each one half of the page. In everything else, he resists. He pinches out every guide-light he passes (shrine candles, lamp niches), so that the follower, whoever he is, will lose the trail. A follower who is lost has not turned his back, so the Overlords do not take him, and he never reaches the Last Stone. Corin cannot put out a rest candle, because it burns with the same fire he carries, so he keeps beyond its glow and lets it see nothing of the children. He never looks back. Lira learned from Wren that a lamplighter never leaves a lamp dark on a road someone will come home by. She re-oils and re-wicks the lamps he darkens, but she has no flame to light them with. She means to keep the way home lit for Tobin. In doing so she keeps the trail for Kael and for the Keeping, and undoes her father's one defiance. Tobin has never known the man and is afraid of him. He pushed his carved dragon under a plank at the river house, where a man walking ahead would not see it. It is the only real call for help on the Road. From the Hollow, Corin went in at the Giant Mangal root door, looked at the lashed stair, and came out again. What he wanted there is for later. He cut through to the Forest of Mangal by the old west track and snapped off its arm on the crossroads sign. He pinched the shrine candles there, and Lira left the bird on the stone. He crossed the Safaris to the river house, crossed the river in the Air house's boat, and slept a night on Wind Hill, where he pressed his ash into the platform and woke the house. Its keeper for twenty years had been Orm, Edda's husband, who rowed the Keeping's supplies to the hill. Four years ago he rowed across for the last time and sent the boat back empty, with his oars shipped inside. Orm rose to Cult Rogue. Three of Dundean's young went up the hill after the priests this season. Edda's grandson was one of them, and his boots are in the terrace hut. At first light the next morning Corin crossed the Safaris to Dundean. Brann and three hunters stood at the valley gate under orders and did not move. A lodge rider had gone up the valley ahead of him to lay three bedrolls and a fire in the drovers' hut, and had come back. Corin laid his ash at the graveyard lichgate and at the edge of the Blood Circle, which woke the Fire house. Its quiet priests that season included Seren, Brann's wife. Eighteen years ago their six-year-old daughter went to Azurelake as a guild apprentice, and a letter came that said fever. Brann is a Keeper. He gave her to the lamps knowing, and he let Seren grieve. Seren buried an empty box beside Brann's father's stone, the one with the hunting horn. Years later she dug it open and found the earth clean, and she never believed the letter again. She knelt in the rite to hear a child who was never under that stone. When the ash came, the bereaved walked down the south track barefoot, the lodge crossed their names off its board in fresh ink, and Seren rose to Blood Rogue. Corin gave each house half of the leaf. Before he tore it, he burned the result's name out with his fingertip, and the heat of his own fire pressed the letters into the paper. Seven years ago he forged Bloodgale himself, and he knows what it is for. He climbed to the red shrine above the pass; why is left open. Apalala did not rise. It cannot rise against the Bearer who holds its binding. It searched the grey man for the father it had once let by, and found nothing of him left, not even the boy. At Longdale, Hild fed the children in her doorway as she had been told, without looking at the Bearer or holding the children. Lira asked her for a cup of lamp oil for the road. At the north gate, Tamsin, the newest of the Keeping, held two guild orders that had come the day before: do not raise a bow to the man, and let the boy through the north gate at whatever hour he comes. Years ago she had hunted these passes with Corin and heard him talk of nothing but his son. She heard the girl say "Father, will Kael be all right?" and the man answer "He always comes." She called him by his name, and he looked at her as if she were a gatepost. He went out of the north gate at dusk toward the Last Stone.

THE FOLLOWER. Kael is the Keeping's chosen successor to his own father. Every bed, meal, kindness and mercy, and every bit of his hatchling's trust, makes him better fuel, because the fire feeds on love. Each candle he rests at is read in Wren's lamp, so his promise to Halvard ("I will send word") is kept without his knowing. The Divine, a Sanctuary spirit that oversees the bindings, appears only to merciful followers and marks them. Mercy chains the Overlords again. When Kael spares Orochi, the Divine relights the Waystone with borrowed light that holds only until the next new moon. If Kael kills Orochi, the Norwoods binding breaks outright. Either way the deadline is the same. The Giant Mangal stair is already torn out, Archelon breaks every boat, and Apalala's pool will not lie still. The Keeping's cruelty prevents a real catastrophe, which is what makes it hard to hate. The only Blood Rogue and Cult Rogue on the Road are the two the houses raised. If Kael captures them to forge Bloodgale, he makes the vessel out of Brann's wife and Edda's husband. This is never said on screen. Halvard's public notice on the Longdale board, "Return the children unharmed. The man is of no account.", does not mention the boy at all. His private order to Tamsin is only about the boy. Later chapters set the final choice. Kael can take the fire: his father falls to ash, the children go home by Wren's lamp, and one day Kael will have to take someone's children himself. He can refuse and become a warden like the Lich, and the island forgets itself. Lira's knots may already have offered her, and nobody, not even Hollin, knows whether the stone honours a knot. There may be a third way no Bearer has found. Nothing is resolved in the current game.

characters.name: Kael
characters.surface: Sixteen. An untrained older brother chasing the man who took his siblings. He believes his father died in the Norwoods seven years ago, looking for him after he wandered off as a boy.
characters.truth: At nine he was the child under the previous Bearer's arm. His father followed him and took the fire. Kael was sent home with the Road wiped from his memory. Now he is the Keeping's chosen successor to that same father, who has burned away every memory of him. His loyalty and mercy make him ideal fuel, and every candle he rests at reports him. If he forges Bloodgale, he makes it from Seren and Orm.
characters.arc: Grief, then resolve. At Edda's thanks he notices she knew about a ribbon he never showed her. At the formula he learns that the page was cut from his own Manual, in Halvard's hand. In the Dundean unlocks he learns that the monsters he fought were Brann's wife and Edda's husband. At Longdale he learns that the Stranger is his father, that Lira went willingly, and that the guild sent word about him before the abduction. He keeps walking anyway, and that stubbornness is exactly what the Keeping relies on.

characters.name: Lira
characters.surface: Nine. Calm and watchful. She leaves a ribbon and a thread to show Kael the way.
characters.truth: She met her father at the West Gate lamps on Wren's rounds and believed him because of the bird he carved her. She lifted the latch herself. She knows he is dying and has decided to 'carry the light after him', which she thinks means becoming a lamplighter. She ties Wren's Dundean name-knot only at stones. She re-oils and re-wicks the lamps he pinches out, using Wren's flask and later Hild's cup, to keep the way home lit for Tobin. She does not know what the fire is or who is meant to inherit it.
characters.arc: Seen only through other people's reports. Later she becomes the cruellest mirror: the child who offered herself to the light in innocence, against the brother walking into it blind.

characters.name: Tobin
characters.surface: Seven. Crying, looking back, holding his sister's hand.
characters.truth: Born the year his father left. To him the man really is a stranger. He hid the dragon Kael carved him under a jetty plank where the man would not see it. It is the only honest call for rescue on the Road.
characters.arc: In a later chapter he goes home by Wren's lamp without Kael, and he is the one who never forgives the Keeping.

characters.name: The Ashen Stranger (Corin, Kael's father)
characters.surface: A man of grey ash who broke three Celestial Rank Hunters, woke an Overlord and stole two children.
characters.truth: The current Bearer, nearly spent, kept alive on the Waystone fire he drank to last until the next new moon. The stone compels him to take the children, walk the Road, wake the trials and hand the page to the houses. In everything else he resists. He pinches out guide-lights so the follower will get lost, burns out the vessel's name, keeps beyond the rest candles' glow, never looks back, and folds the children's blankets. He means for no one to take the fire. He bargained away his memory of Kael to keep his love for the two children he had to carry, so he does not know the follower is his son. 'He always comes' is the Book speaking, not a father.
characters.arc: Never seen, and never speaks in the current game except in reported speech. Unmasked by Tamsin at Longdale. Later he meets his son at the Last Stone and asks who he is.

characters.name: Master Halvard
characters.surface: A stern, grieving guild master who tries to stop Kael, then arms him out of respect for his father.
characters.truth: Head of the Keeping in Azurelake. He let his own son Ivo follow fourteen years ago and become Bearer, and Ivo's dragon is chained at the pass because of it. He chose Kael's family seven years ago and again now. He hand-wrote the Manual's last page, including the line that a companion will follow 'even into the dark', and he cut the formula leaf from it. He brought the Celestials to be broken and sent letters ahead to Dundean and Longdale before the abduction. His warning at the stairs is the Road's first required refusal. He loves Kael, and he would do all of it again.
characters.arc: Absent after the opening, but present in every lamp and page. Revealed through his handwriting at the formula and his orders at Longdale. In a later chapter he answers for it face to face.

characters.name: Wren
characters.surface: The kind lamplighter who keeps Lira's lamp lit and passes on hints.
characters.truth: A Keeping lamplighter who reads the rest candles in the fountain lamp. Seven years ago, at seventeen, she found Kael asleep under the West Gate lamp. She refilled the west lamps, took Lira to meet her father, taught her the knot and gave her the oil flask. 'Travellers say' the Waystone went dark is her one lie: the road was closed, and she read it in the light. She is Brann and Seren's daughter, taken from Dundean at six. She has forgotten Dundean, but she still ties its name-knot and says its farewell, 'keep to the trail'. She believes the Keeping saves the island.
characters.arc: Every line she says is tender, and all but one is literally true. In a later chapter she waits at the fountain with blankets for two children, not three, and learns what her mother became.

characters.name: Old Edda
characters.surface: Dundean's innkeeper. A free bed, food, gruff care. She lends her husband's oars for the Wind Hill mission.
characters.truth: Keeper of the Dundean way-house for forty years. She fed Corin seven years ago and Ivo before him. She had Halvard's letter describing the boy and his sister's ribbon before Kael arrived. Her husband Orm rowed the Keeping's supplies to the Air house for twenty years. Four years ago he sent the boat back empty with the oars inside, and stayed. He is the Cult Rogue. Her grandson went up after him this season and did not come down. 'I cannot tell you what it is for' is true: she is not permitted to.
characters.arc: She slips about the ribbon in her thanks, and when Kael catches it she will not explain ('Not mine to tell, boy. Eat first.'). In the same breath she confesses her husband and grandson. 'Keep the oars' means she wants nothing of him back in her house.

characters.name: Brann
characters.surface: An honest gatekeeper hunter who bars the valley, sends Kael to break the rite over his father's grave, then hauls away the pine.
characters.truth: Keeper of the Fire house's lodge, as his father was before him. He does not lie, but he withholds. He opens each bar on the Keeping's schedule. He gave his own daughter to the lamps knowing she would live, and he let his wife grieve an empty grave for eighteen years. Three nights before Kael arrives, Seren walked down barefoot to the rite, and Brann crossed her name off the board himself. He sent a stranger because he could not lift a blade against her.
characters.arc: 'My father's stone is still standing. Thank you, Kael' is said knowing whose hand was on the grave beside it. He confesses Seren in the same conversation, opens the road anyway, and cannot finish 'come back the same way you leave'.

characters.name: Seren (the Blood Rogue)
characters.surface: The heart of the blood rite: 'patient, not afraid'.
characters.truth: Brann's wife and Wren's mother. She went to the rite to hear the daughter she believed dead, a daughter who was never under that stone. She wears a ring cut from the same horn as Brann's family stone. 'I was a priest once. Like them.'
characters.arc: Spared, she puts out the fire with her own hand and walks into the dark between the stones. Defeated, she is gone from the dais. Captured, she is in Kael's company, unrecognised. In every outcome Brann loses her in this chapter.

characters.name: Orm (the Cult Rogue)
characters.surface: Leader of the wind priests. 'They kneel because I kneel.'
characters.truth: Edda's husband, keeper and ferryman of the Air house for twenty years. His oars and the far jetty's mooring post carry the same small burned wheel. He kneels to the Bearer, and his followers kneel because he does.
characters.arc: In this chapter he scatters into the wind, falls, or is captured. Edda confesses him in her thanks.

characters.name: Hild
characters.surface: Longdale innkeeper who fed the children in her doorway.
characters.truth: Keeper of the Longdale house. She was told not to look at the Bearer and not to hold the children, and she obeyed. She gave Lira a cup of lamp oil 'for the road'. She saw the guild notice go up the day before the man came.
characters.arc: She sends Kael to Tamsin knowing what Tamsin heard.

characters.name: Tamsin
characters.surface: The north gatekeeper who 'did not raise her bow'.
characters.truth: The newest of the Keeping, and the one who broke. Years ago she hunted the Earlsome passes with Corin. She heard the girl call him Father and name Kael, and when she called him by his name he did not know her. She holds a guild order to let the boy through at any hour. She disobeys it the only way she can, by keeping the dale-ward law and barring the gate until dawn.
characters.arc: Delivers the father reveal and the order in her first conversation. In a later chapter she is Kael's first possible ally against the Keeping.

characters.name: Maren and Osk
characters.surface: Ringfeld shelter keepers who send Kael back east and warn him off the causeway.
characters.truth: Keepers of the Lighthouse, the Keeping's clock. The well-cap carries a column of year-marks, evenly spaced, one for each time the light went dark. The newest has no year, and below it the stone is smoothed ready. The crushed boat was Maren's son's: he tried to cross past Archelon and relight the Lighthouse.
characters.arc: Frontier only. Maren's seven-year line gives the cycle and the deadline. A later chapter brings Kael across the causeway.

characters.name: The Lich (Hollin)
characters.surface: An undead scholar who warns Kael to turn back.
characters.truth: Founder of the Keeping and author of the Book of the Road. He was the first to refuse the fire at the Last Stone, and the stone made him the undying warden of the first warning. The name the Stranger spoke was his own. His warning is sincere, and it is also the ritual that makes going on count as consent. Seven years ago he saw a sleeping nine-year-old carried past, and a father running after him.
characters.arc: Spared, he hints that he has seen Kael before. Killed, he leaves only dread. Either way his books, which hold the full Book of the Road, survive for a later chapter. 'Dark Matter' is what waits for those who refuse at the end.

characters.name: Orochi
characters.surface: The Overlord the Stranger woke to block the road.
characters.truth: Once Noko. Bound in burning pain inside the Waystone for a century, and dragged south to it when the Bearer drank the stone dark. It bargained for a few hours free and for the Book's term: the first follower who turns his back.
characters.arc: Spared, it sinks back into its chain and its pain, and the Divine praises Kael for it. Killed, it whispers '...free...', the Norwoods binding breaks, and the Waystone stays dark.

characters.name: Divine
characters.surface: A kind celestial that rewards mercy and points the way.
characters.truth: A spirit of the Sanctuary that oversees the bindings. It appears only to merciful followers and marks them as the best fuel. Every word it says is true, and each one steers Kael along the Road. It relights the stone only until the next new moon. It is not evil: it values the island's order above any one family.
characters.arc: Its 'He makes bargains' pays off when Corin's forgetting is revealed, and again at the Last Stone.

characters.name: Apalala
characters.surface: The Dragon Overlord guarding the pass, which let the Stranger by but fought Kael.
characters.truth: Ivo's Blue Wyrm, Halvard's son's companion, raised from a guild Water Hatchling and named after the river spirit of the lake tales. When the fire burned their bond fourteen years ago, it tried to follow Ivo in, and it was raised into an Overlord and chained to the pass. It cannot rise against the Bearer who holds its binding. Seven years ago it watched Ivo carry a sleeping boy past and a father come after him. Now it found nothing of that father left, not even the boy. It checks Kael's hands for ash, to see whether he is a Bearer yet.
characters.arc: '...Not even you.' Its head tilts like a hatchling's when Kael speaks of the lake at home. Who it was is revealed in a later chapter, and its chain becomes a choice.

twists.twist: THE LAST PAGE: the trials were written for Kael by the people helping him. Both formula halves are in Halvard's brown-ink hand, on a leaf cut from the Manual he gave Kael. And Edda knew about Lira's ribbon, which Kael never showed her.

main.scenes.items_handover: 'Ask at Dundean first... Someone always sees.' The witnesses were arranged
main.scenes.guild_hall_choice_intro: the hatchlings 'hatched last week', ready before anyone had reason to need them

missions.fragments.*.found: 'careful and even, in brown ink'. MenuScene.ts lines 254-255 must say the same (see beat sheet)
missions.done.blood[4] (Brann): 'Someone made that page, and someone gave it to them to guard.' He knows who
missions.done.wind[3] (Edda): 'That hand is old, and steady.' This describes Halvard
missions.done.wind[5] (Edda): 'Keep it with your sister's ribbon.' The ribbon has been in Kael's coat since the Waystone, and he never names it in Dundean
missions.formula.page: 'perform the formula on the last page.' The only book Kael owns with a hand-written last page is the Manual
twists.reveal_at: The ribbon slip is caught at once, in regions.unlock_lines.giant_mangal_f2, which plays straight after missions.done.wind. The handwriting is revealed in missions.formula.joined, whichever hill gives the second half.
twists.why_it_makes_sense: The page is physical evidence. Its ink and hand match 'A Last Word', and its inner edge fits the cut stub, so it existed before the abduction and passed through Halvard's hands. Edda's knowledge comes from Halvard's letter, sent before the abduction, describing the boy who would come. Kael can check it against every line he spoke in Dundean. Rest candles inside enemy trials only make sense if someone tends them. Neither half of the reveal depends on the other, so it works in either mission order.

twists.twist: DUNDEAN'S OWN: the Blood Priests and wind priests were Dundean's bereaved, kept in the Keeping's trial houses. The Blood Rogue at the altar was Brann's wife Seren. The Cult Rogue was Edda's husband, and her grandson's boots are in the terrace hut. Brann and Edda sent Kael against their own family. Because no other Rogues exist on the Road, the two Kael must capture for Bloodgale are them.

twists.why_it_makes_sense: The game already shows these creatures as a line of growth (priest, then warrior, then rogue) and says they 'were priests once'. The houses were 'few and quiet for years' and woke only when the ash came. Every physical clue points to living villagers walking in: bare feet, hands on family graves, names freshly struck out, Dundean boots, the oar mark on the cult's jetty. Both quest-givers hesitate in their own words. A wife or husband is exactly the person you would ask a stranger to fight.

twists.twist: THE GIRL CALLED HIM FATHER: the Ashen Stranger is Corin, Kael's father, believed dead for seven years. Lira went with him willingly. And he no longer knows who Kael is.

She asks Kael's name, then: 'The girl held his sleeve at this gate and said: Father, will Kael be all right? He said: He always comes.' / 'I called him by his name. He looked at me as if I were a gatepost.' Kael: '...Father.' The forgetting is only implied; its full reveal is for a later chapter.
twists.why_it_makes_sense: Everything fits a dying parent, and nothing fits a kidnapper. The children walk freely and sleep beside him, the camp was laid ready, the hunters were spared, Lira thanks people and opened the door herself, and the carving carries a family knife-mark. The early clues point at Kael's past without naming the man. 'He always comes' reads as a father's faith the first time, and as the Book's indifference once the player sets it beside 'as if I were a gatepost', 'Not even you' and Orochi's promised boy.

twists.twist: THE HUNT IS FOR KAEL: the Stranger is the dying Bearer of the Waystones' fire, and only someone who follows out of love and refuses every warning can inherit it. The children were always going home. Bloodgale is the vessel for the handover, which is why his father burned its name. Every candle Kael rests at reports him, every mercy chains an Overlord again, and the deadline is the next new moon.

twists.why_it_makes_sense: It explains every remaining oddity. The kidnapper is followed but never ambushed, leaves wardens instead of traps, and erases a formula he was handed. The abduction is staged with hunters set up to lose. Companions are hatched in advance, and the helpers feed and train the pursuer. Overlords let the Stranger pass and test the boy. People in Dundean know things Kael never said. The guild's orders reached Longdale too fast to have been sent after the abduction, and they care about the children and the boy while dismissing the man. Love is the fire's fuel, which is why the Keeping is kind. The failing bindings give the Keeping a real and terrible reason.

twists.twist: HE ONLY KNOWS WHICH WAY THE ROAD GOES: Kael has walked this road before. At nine he was the child under the previous Bearer's arm. His father followed him and took the fire, which is how Corin became the Stranger. Kael was sent home with the Road wiped from his memory.

twists.why_it_makes_sense: Kael's family story, a lost boy and a father who died searching for him, is exactly what the Keeping would tell the town. The forgetting is written on the stone itself. The Lich, who never leaves the Mosswood, and Apalala, who never leaves the pass, would both have seen the boy carried past. The Lighthouse's seven years line up with the year his father vanished.

twists.twist: LIRA'S KNOTS AND OIL: Lira's ribbon and thread are not signals to Kael. They are a Dundean name-knot Wren taught her, the same knot the rite ties into its red cloths for the dead, and she ties them only at stones to give her name to the light in her father's place. She re-oils and re-wicks every lamp her father darkens, from Wren's flask and Hild's cup, and so keeps the trail lit for the Keeping, undoing his one defiance.

twists.why_it_makes_sense: The knot rule (a knot is a name given) is shown by the rite before it matters. The knots appear only at stones. A guild-oil lantern deep in the Norwoods can only have been filled by someone who left Azurelake that night, and the man darkens lamps rather than filling them. Lira knows her father is dying and always wanted to light the lamps herself. Her love and Kael's, each acting in ignorance, are both used by the Keeping.

twists.twist: APALALA IS HALVARD'S SON'S DRAGON: the Dragon Overlord of the pass is the Blue Wyrm of Ivo, Halvard's son and the Bearer before Corin. Raised from a guild Water Hatchling, it was chained there when it tried to follow its tamer into the fire. Seven years ago it saw a sleeping boy carried past and a father running after him, and it remembers the boy.

twists.why_it_makes_sense: Apalala is the only Overlord that speaks of a former self ('I was'), and that former form is a tamed dragon's final stage. It lets the ash pass without rising, looks for ash on Kael's hands, and knows the grey man once had something of Kael to give away. Making it Ivo's, not Corin's, explains why Kael does not recognise his own father's dragon. It also turns Halvard's hand-written promise, that a companion follows 'even into the dark', into his own son's story.

twists.twist: WREN IS BRANN'S DAUGHTER: the empty grave beside the horn stone belongs to a girl the guild took from Dundean at six to be a lamplighter. The letter said fever. She is Wren, who has forgotten Dundean but still ties its knot and says its farewell. Brann always knew.

twists.why_it_makes_sense: The Keeping takes one child per house per generation for the lamps, and the light takes the road home out of lamplighters, which is also why returned children forget. A Dundean mourning knot taught by an Azurelake lamplighter, and a Dundean farewell in her mouth, can only come from someone raised there first. The ages fit: six when taken eighteen years ago, seventeen when she found Kael. Kael has no reason to know where Wren came from, because she arrived before he was born. The player can see it and Kael cannot.

cruel_beats: main.scenes.wake_aftermath: the latch was lifted from inside. Kael assumes the Stranger forced Lira; she opened the door for her father. Her oil flask is gone because she means to keep the road lit.
main.scenes.guildmaster_stops_you: the choice is fake. Both answers are his father's words from seven years ago, and either one counts as consent to the Road.

main.items.manual 'A Last Word': the guild master's hand-written promise that a companion will follow 'even into the dark' is the story of his own son's dragon, now chained at the pass Kael must cross.
Every rest at a candle, the game's save point, keeps Kael's promise 'I will send word' and reports him to the people who built his trials.

expansion.after_orochi_peace: the kindest act in the game sends Orochi back into a century of burning, a radiant spirit thanks him for it, and the relit stone holds only until the next new moon. Killing it instead makes it whisper '...free...'.
missions.fights.blood_rite_rows: 'These are Dundean's dead. Get your hands off them.' They were Dundean's living, with their hands on their own families' graves.

missions.fights.blood_rite_altar: 'Whatever he promised you, it ends here.' A mother wearing her husband's family horn, kneeling to hear a daughter who was never in the ground, and whom her husband knew was alive.

missions.done.blood + unlock: 'My father's stone is still standing. Thank you, Kael.' Brann already knows whose hand was on the empty grave beside it, because he crossed her name off the board himself. He holds it in for one breath, then confesses.

missions.offer.wind / done.wind: Edda hands Kael the oars her husband sent home empty, so that he can row across and break him. Then she says 'keep the oars'. The boots in the hut were her grandson's; he went up to bring his grandfather home.
done.wind + unlock: Edda, thanking him, says 'your sister's ribbon', and Kael realises he never showed it to her.
missions.formula.joined: the man who placed a trusting hatchling in his arms wrote the trials, on a leaf cut from Kael's own Manual.

Satchel fusion (unspoken): no other Blood Rogue or Cult Rogue exists on the Road. To forge Bloodgale, Kael must bind Brann's wife and Edda's husband and make them one, as the vessel his father burned the name to hide. The father's single act of defiance was undone first by the heat of his own fire, and then by his son's diligence.
Lira's oil: the father pinches out every light so the follower will get lost and be spared; the daughter he loves re-lights the trail behind him so her brother will be caught.
regions.bosses.apalala.after_peace: a chained dragon that once let a father run after his son says of the grey man: '...Not even you.'
regions.npc_dialogue.tamsin: 'Father, will Kael be all right?' 'He always comes.' Kael hears faith. It is a man reciting a rule about a stranger.

things_generated.longdale_square.guild_board + Tamsin's order: the guild's public word is 'The man is of no account', and its private order, sent before the abduction, is to hurry the boy through the gate. Halvard dismisses Kael's father in writing.
expansion.room_entries.safaris_riverbank: Tobin's dragon, hidden from the man, is the only sign on the whole Road that really means 'save me', and it came from the child who did not know him.
Later: the guilt Kael carried all his life, that his father died looking for him, was true in the worst possible way, and his father does not remember him.
Later: Lira and Tobin walk into Azurelake by the lamp Wren kept lit, and Wren has blankets for two. Wren learns her mother knelt eighteen years to hear her.
Later: the Bearer's bond burns first. Kael's hatchling, raised from level one, will be the first thing the fire takes, and it will try to follow him, like Apalala.

rules: Fixed on-screen names: Kael (16), Lira (9), Tobin (7), Master Halvard, Wren, Old Edda, Brann, Hild, Tamsin, Maren, Osk, the Ashen Stranger. Internal names: Corin (father), Ivo (Halvard's son, the previous Bearer and Apalala's tamer), Hollin (the Lich), Seren (Brann's wife, the Blood Rogue), Orm (Edda's husband, the Cult Rogue). The only internal name that may appear on screen is 'Seren', spoken by Brann in regions.unlock_lines.south_earlsome_valley. Edda says only 'my husband' and 'my grandson'. Tamsin says 'Father' (quoting Lira) and 'his name', never 'Corin'. The words Keeping, Bearer, Last Stone, vessel and Book of the Road never appear on screen. No names are cut into the Ringfeld well-cap.

CODE CONSTRAINTS. (1) A plain NPC's `first` plays once; after that, each talk shows one random `repeat` line. There are no second conversations. Every reveal goes in `first` (or in mission/unlock lines), and repeat lines must be self-contained, order-independent and spoiler-safe. (2) For Brann and Edda, `first` is prepended to the mission offer. done[m] and that mission's unlock lines play back to back in one dialogue, so unlock lines continue the same conversation. (3) formula.joined fires in the field the moment the second fragment is picked up, which may be on either hill and may come before or after the other giver's done lines. So formula.joined must not refer to anything said in done or unlock lines, and done or unlock lines must not assume the formula is joined. (4) Mission fight `after` lines play whatever the outcome (killed, spared or captured) and must be outcome-neutral; only spare_text is outcome-specific. (5) Room entries play on first visit only; landmark text plays on every examine. (6) The ringfeld_lower_road unlock lines never play. (7) There is no day/night cycle. Longdale is always at dusk, and its north gate is a permanent frontier. (8) Blood Rogue and Cult Rogue exist only in the mission fights, so the Bloodgale fusion always uses the houses' own Rogues. (9) MenuScene.ts formula page text must be changed to brown ink and the same hand.

What Kael knows. From the start until Dundean: a kidnapping, and that his father died looking for him when he was small. After Edda's thanks: she knew about a ribbon he never showed her. At the formula: Halvard wrote the page, on a leaf cut from Kael's own Manual, but not why. After each giver's thanks: the rite and the cult were Dundean's own, the Blood Rogue was Brann's wife and the Cult Rogue was Edda's husband. At Longdale: the Stranger is his father, Lira went willingly, and the guild's order about him came the day before his father did. He must NOT learn, or conclude, that he is the intended successor, that he was carried this road at nine, what Bloodgale is for, that the fused Rogues were Seren and Orm, what the knots or the oil mean, that the candles report him, that mercy chains the Overlords, whose dragon Apalala was, that Wren is Brann's daughter, or that his father has forgotten him.

Corin's forgetting of Kael is only implied in the current game, through Orochi's 'first to follow', Apalala's '...Not even you', Tamsin's 'as if I were a gatepost' and 'He always comes'. Never state it.
Edda's knowledge of the ribbon comes from Halvard's letter, sent before the abduction. Only lamplighters (Wren) can read the candles. No Dundean or Longdale keeper reads lights.
The Divine and the Overlords never lie, but they speak partially. Every Divine line must be literally true and must steer Kael onward.

The helpers' kindness is sincere. No Keeper sneers, gloats or admits the plan. The only flat lie in the game is Wren's 'Travellers say'. Edda's 'I cannot tell you' and 'Not mine to tell', and Brann's 'not mine to say', are refusals, not lies. Brann never claims his daughter is dead. Edda and Brann confess their own kin, but neither confirms nor denies Halvard's design. They deflect, still feed Kael, and still open the roads.

The order of the Book: a follower who turns back before passing the Lich goes home. Passing the Lich is consent, and turning one's back after that belongs to the Overlords. A follower who is lost or late is not taken by the Overlords and does not reach the Last Stone, which is what Corin wants. The stone takes only someone who set out in ignorance and who takes the fire by his own hand once told. The four warnings (Halvard, Lich, Orochi, Apalala) are never commented on as a pattern.

Lights. Rest candles burn with the Road's own fire. The Stranger cannot put them out, keeps beyond their glow, and they see whoever rests beside them. Guide-lights (shrine candles, lamp niches, trail lanterns) gutter near him on their own, and pinched wicks are his deliberate act. Lira re-oils and re-wicks guide-lights but has no flame to light them. Wren keeps the Azurelake and outskirts lamps. The Safaris waymarker lantern is kept by Dundean's house. These rules must hold in every room.

Ash is the Bearer's body burning off. It is cold, and it marks where he lingered or laid a hand: the Waystone, the Mangal root door, the lichgate, the Blood Circle's edge, the Wind Hill platform and hut, the drovers' hut, the red shrine ledge, the Longdale cobbles and gate. The Ringfeld ash went up on the wind the night he drank the Waystone's fire. The West Gate's claw marks and blood belong to the Celestials' dragons and the hunters themselves; the Stranger has no companion.

Knots: each of the rite's red cloths carries a knot for a name. Lira's ribbon and thread use the same knot and appear only at stones. Whether the stone honours them stays ambiguous. Lira believes 'carry the light' means becoming a lamplighter.

The Stranger's route and timing. New moon night: abduction, Mosswood an hour before dawn, Waystone. Day 1: Serpent's Hollow camp, Mangal root door, the old west track to the crossroads (the snapped fourth arm), river house. Night 2: Wind Hill. Dawn of day 3: across the Safaris and through the valley gate; ash at the lichgate; the rite wakes that night; drovers' hut. Day 4: the pass, Longdale at evening, out of the north gate at dusk. Kael reaches Dundean about three mornings after the Stranger passed it, because training and resting cost him days. Halvard's orders reached Longdale by the long road through Wesing on day 3, which is only possible if they were sent before the abduction. The handover deadline is the next new moon, about a month after the abduction, and is foreshadowed only.

Both Orochi outcomes are canon. Spared: the Waystone burns on borrowed light until the next new moon, and Orochi is chained again. Killed: Orochi whispers '...free...', the Waystone stays dark and the Norwoods binding is broken. Both Lich outcomes leave his books for later. The Rogue outcomes (spared, defeated, captured) are all canon. In every case Brann and Edda have lost them, and later chapters must honour whichever happened.

Only the Dundean houses' priests, warriors and Rogues were Dundean people. Never state or imply that wild Blood or Cult creatures elsewhere are human. On screen, never confirm or deny that a captured or fused Rogue was Seren or Orm. Later chapters treat it as true. What becomes of the rite's people who fall is left open. They do not get up as people, and no bodies are described.

DIB facts stay unchanged: Orochi evolved from Noko; Apalala is a Dragon Overlord whose true form is a Blue Wyrm (in-world, 'Apalala' is the name Ivo gave his hatchling, after the river spirit of the lake tales); the Divine is a spirit of the Sanctuary; Bloodgale is Blood Rogue + Cult Rogue; the evolution levels are as given in the Manual. Bloodgale's role as the Book's vessel is in-world belief only and is never stated in the current game. Dark Mage and Dark Priest do not appear; they are hinted at only through the Lich's 'Dark Matter will find you'. The barbarian, al-Rashid, Cyrus, Iris and the breeders stay as DIB world flavour and are not tied to the Keeping.

Ages and dates: Ivo followed fourteen years ago. Corin took the fire seven years ago, when Kael was 9, Lira 2 and Tobin newly born. The mother died two winters ago (cause left open). Wren was taken from Dundean at six, eighteen years ago, and was seventeen when she found Kael. The Lighthouse goes dark for one moon every seven years. Orm stayed on the hill four years ago.

Left open: the Last Stone's location (north of Longdale); what lives on Giant Mangal floor 4 and above; what the Stranger wanted in the Mangal and at the red shrine; what became of Corin's own companion; what kept the pass before Apalala; whether the rite's promise to let the bereaved hear their dead is real; whether Halvard or the Divine steered Corin's bargain; whether the Divine is benevolent; whether Halvard will turn; whether the cycle can be broken.

The legacy ending_* scenes in main.json are unused and must not resolve anything. Nothing ends. The last current-game beat is Kael at Longdale's barred north gate, knowing his father lives, with the hunt continuing at dawn.

Tone: sober and literal. No jokes, no gore, nothing sexual. Cruelty comes only from betrayal, irony, loss, recognition and choices. Re-read lines must stay true. Kael's guesses may be wrong about motive but must never contradict a physical fact.
